citeAs: The EgoLife Team (2025). EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv:2503.03803.
creator: Jingkang Yang, Shuai Liu, Yuhao Dong, Binzhu Xie, Zitang Zhou, Ziyue Wang, Bei Ouyang, Zhengyu Lin, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang, Joerg Widmer, Xiamengwei Zhang, Hongming Guo, Pengyun Wang, Sicheng Zhang, Marco Cominelli, Francesco Gringoli, Bo Li, Yuanhan Zhang, Peiyuan Zhang, Fangzhou Hong, Ziwei Liu (LMMs-Lab, NTU S-Lab)
description: EgoLife is a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation. It was collected over one week with six participants living together, continuously recording daily activities using Meta Aria glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references from 15 GoPro cameras and 2 mmWave devices. The dataset includes rich annotations such as audio transcripts, visual-audio narrations, and the EgoLifeQA benchmark for long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks.
name: EgoLife Dataset
rai:annotationsPerItem: Caption annotations: 361K brief narration phrases merged into 25K merged captions, then expanded into visual-audio captions. EgoLifeQA: 500 QA per participant (3,000 total across 6 participants), filtered from ~100K AI-generated candidates per participant (less than 1% retained).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut (ByteDance) video editing software with dubbing functions was used for caption annotation. SRT files were used for QA annotation review, allowing annotators to view questions in sync with video segments.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three annotation types: (1) Transcript: Audio from six participants merged, speech recognition applied, diarization algorithm used to differentiate speakers, then manually reviewed and refined per participant track. (2) Captions: Videos split into 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8x speed; annotators provided continuous narrations covering all actions, interactions, and environmental details; narrations converted to text and reviewed. GPT-4o-mini merged 361K brief phrases into 25K merged captions; GPT-4o expanded these into visual-audio captions using representative frames (1 FPS) and transcripts; human annotators verified. (3) EgoLifeQA: GPT-4o generated ~100K timestamped QA candidates per participant from visual-audio captions; annotators reviewed as SRT files synced with video; only questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior retained; filtered to 1K high-quality questions per participant, then refined to 500 QA per participant; annotators also generated distractors for multiple-choice questions and annotated audio requirement and look-back time.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is intentionally narrow in scope (single language, single scenario) to build a strong foundation, which limits generalizability. The primary language is Chinese, with only one English-language session. All participants lived in the same house for a specific themed event (Earth Day celebration), which may not represent typical daily life. The dataset involves only six participants, limiting demographic diversity. Activity categorization was automatically performed using GPT-4o, which may introduce model-specific biases.
rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together for one week in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos (~8 hours/day). 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data. Participants performed daily activities including discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment. Recording permission was obtained for locations outside the house such as shopping malls. Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes: first-person egocentric video and audio from 6 Meta Aria glasses (VRS format), third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras (Beijing) / 6 GoPro cameras (Milan), IMU data (CSV), gaze data (CSV), millimeter-wave radar ADC data (CSV), and WiFi channel state information (HDF5, Milan only). Video+Audio stored as MP4, annotations as JSON.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day period (one week); Beijing session. A one-day session in Milan was also conducted. The Beijing dataset is the primary dataset discussed in the paper.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset starts with a narrow setting sacrificing some generalizability (single language/scenario). The primary language is Chinese (with one English session). Limited to six participants in a single shared living environment. Recording gaps occur every three hours when glasses are collected for data upload (approximately one hour gap). The dataset currently covers only two environments (Beijing and Milan). Future plans include expanding to broader range of languages, locations, and activities.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed for annotation. Activity categorization automatically performed using GPT-4o on visual-audio captions with timestamps. Audio split into six separate tracks (one per participant) for transcript annotation. Videos processed into 30-second clips for EgoGPT captioning in EgoButler pipeline.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data processing pipeline (EgoSync) synchronizes multi-source data (video, audio, IMU) from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras. EgoBlur applies privacy protection by blurring all participant faces, bystander faces, and vehicle license plates. Audio muting is applied to sensitive audio segments. Screen content with private information is blurred. Multi-view synchronization aligns video and signal data using timestamps. mmWave data post-processed using constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection algorithm. WiFi CSI data collected and processed using AX-CSI platform.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is described as ongoing, with plans to expand to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities. The Milan dataset (EgoLife-Milan) has been collected and will be detailed in an upcoming EgoLife blog series. The annotation team partnership will continue for future EgoLife versions. The dataset card describes it as an "ongoing project."
rai:dataSocialImpact: EgoButler and EgoLifeQA could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life especially for individuals needing consistent support such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges. In educational and professional settings, egocentric AI could facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development. The technology raises privacy and ethical considerations requiring safeguards for data privacy and transparency in AI decision-making. The project aims to foster AI companions capable of supporting individuals in a socially and ethically responsible manner.
rai:dataUseCases: Development of egocentric life AI assistants; long-context video understanding; multimodal egocentric video understanding; identity recognition and tracking; long-context question answering (EgoLifeQA tasks: EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster); human behavior recognition; multimodal signal analysis; human-machine interaction; studying long-duration activities, interpersonal dynamics, and contextual interactions; training omni-modal models for egocentric data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o-mini (merging narration phrases into captions), GPT-4o (expanding merged captions into visual-audio captions; generating ~100K QA candidates per participant; activity categorization using visual-audio captions with timestamps), Whisper (speech recognition for transcript generation), open-source diarization algorithm (speaker diarization)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains recordings of participants' daily lives including personal activities, conversations, and interactions. Privacy measures applied include: blurring of all participant faces and bystander faces, blurring of vehicle license plates, muting of sensitive audio segments containing private or potentially identifiable information, and blurring of sensitive screen content (passwords, personal data). All participants provided informed consent. Raw data stored securely with anonymization applied.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper does not describe the demographics (age, gender, nationality, expertise level) of the annotation team beyond naming some team members and their institutional affiliations.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper does not report inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis. It describes a rigorous selection process (filtering 100K to 500 QAs per participant) but no formal IAA statistics.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper describes recording gaps (glasses collected every 3 hours for ~1 hour) but does not explicitly discuss handling of missing data in the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described in the paper; missing data handling is not discussed.
